text:
morgan: heads-up — saw a regression today on the 8xA100 pool after the kernel-selector change. Several requests triggered soft OOMs during batch assembly when long-prefix chat histories were common. stack traces and pprof attached below. trying to triage whether this is a batching admission bug or kv-cache estimator mismatch.

lee: saw the alerts. do you have a minimal repro? was this with `kernel=v1.4-opt` fallback behavior?

morgan: repro is small: many concurrent chat completions with ~1.2k prefix tokens and a 4k generation budget. admission allowed large batches, runtime tried `v1.4-opt` kernel which uses a memory-heavy fused-kv path. pprof shows sudden spike in device memory during KV materialization. snippet: ```# pprof heap
Total: 94GB
kv_buffers: 48GB
batch_inputs: 28GB
other: 18GB```

anita: interesting — kernel-selector recently started preferring fused kernels for 1-2 token latency wins. fused path allocates contiguous kv buffers instead of fragmented pages which can spike committed memory. could be fragmentation + high per-request kv footprints. :thinking: 

perf-bot: regression detector: batch-assembly-time increased 12% over baseline; OOMs from host->device staging: +3 incidents in last 2 hours.

sam: quick thought: our admission currently uses `batch_token_budget` only. we never account for per-request `kv_estimate` which depends on prefix length and model layer size. need to switch to a composite budget: tokens + kv_bytes.

dina: agree. propose: when considering admitting request into batch, compute `estimated_kv = prefix_tokens * kv_per_token_factor` (profiled per-model), then check `batch_kv_sum + estimated_kv <= kv_headroom_threshold` in addition to token budget. if exceeded, either delay or route to kernel with lower kv footprint.

morgan: +1. also want dynamic per-queue thresholds: on A100 we can be more aggressive, on T4 smaller headrooms. and add a fast-path check: if any single request `estimated_kv > single_request_limit` reject early with 413 to client (so we don't OOM).

lee: implementation detail: where to store `kv_per_token_factor`? model profile DB? or compute on first request and cache? computing on first request involves a quick dry-run may be expensive.

anita: store in model metadata at onboarding/profile time. we have perf traces per model already — add a small field `kv_per_tok` and `kernel_kv_multiplier` (fused vs split). fallback policy: if fused would exceed headroom, prefer split-kernel or quantized-kernel.

sam: also watch for kernel selection hysteresis. if we route to split-kernel too often we'll regress latency. add a cost function: prefer fused only if kv_headroom - estimated_kv > fused_safety_margin. else choose split-kernel.

morgan: noted. small config example for queue policy: ```queue_policy: 
  batch_token_limit: 4096
  kv_headroom_bytes: 48GB
  per_model_kv_per_tok: 40B
  fused_safety_margin: 6GB
  single_request_kv_limit: 12GB```

dina: plus metrics: emit `batch_kv_estimate`, `batch_kv_headroom`, `admit_reject_reason` so we can tune margins with real traffic. also expose `kernel_choice_reason` for postmortems.

lee: quick experiment plan: 1) enable kv-aware admission on a small canary (10% of requests on a single pool). 2) set conservative margins (fused_safety_margin=8GB). 3) monitor OOMs and p50/p95 latency. rollback if latency regresses >15%.

morgan: started canary config PR: will push soon. adding a small synthetic test that generates many long-prefix chats to validate admission.

anita: one more gotcha — cuda mem fragmentation can make headroom estimates optimistic. we should subtract an empirical fragmentation penalty per-GPU (from nightly defrag traces). e.g., effective_headroom = kv_headroom_bytes * (1 - frag_factor).

sam: good call. frag_factor for some A100 instances is ~0.12 after prolonged churn. include that in canary.

morgan: thanks all. I'll push the PR and post the link. if we see OOMs persist after kv-aware admission + kernel fallback, we'll instrument per-batch kv allocation and add soft-eviction as last resort. :thumbsup:
